correctness.rationale: The hub is isolated in the complement so it cannot be zero. With hub one, the trace of the ordered-pair transfer matrix counts cyclic Roman words once for each labeled word with its fixed start. A zero needs both a selected rim neighbor and a selected rim nonneighbor. For zero rim twos only the all-one rim is possible; for one there can be no zeros, giving the first replacement; for two only the exactly-one-neighbor positions are free, giving F_{n,|X_S|} in place of F_{n,|U_S|}. With three or more twos the complement condition is automatic since a zero has only two rim neighbors. With hub two there is no wheel constraint on rim zeros: zero twos gives all ones, one two forces its two neighbors to one, two twos force just their common neighbors to one, and three or more allows every nonselected position to be free. This yields the frozen polynomial, including n=3 and the four-cycle with two common neighbors for opposite vertices. For n≥8 hub-one weight is at least n−1 in the two-support case and exceeds six in all other cases. Hub-two weight six is attained by the n one-support labelings and exactly those pairs without a common rim neighbor, of which there are (n choose 2)−n. Independent full labeled-graph enumeration through n=9 and a separate minima check through n=12 reproduce the small-order table and optimizer types. The supplied C++ file prints rather than asserts its minima; the independent enumeration and the symbolic case proof substantiate them.
residual_risks: The supplied scripts were read, not run. Small-order enumeration is corroboration of the proof, not the all-order argument.

value.rationale: The ordinary cycle polynomial and known wheel minima do not determine the full labeled joint distribution by weight and number of rim defenders. The formula identifies exactly where the complement changes the ordinary count and provides all coefficients uniformly. The resulting eventual a priori optimizer count and split into the two hub-two families are a useful extremal consequence, not a claim that the known scalar minimum is new.
residual_risks: No extension to arbitrary hub graphs or to orbit counts is claimed.
